record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.original_question: For disjoint zero sequences A and B in the unit disk, let I(A) and I(B) be the zero-based invariant subspaces of L2_a(D) consisting of functions vanishing on A and B, respectively. For which pairs of disjoint zero sequences A and B is the algebraic sum I(A) + I(B) dense in L2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: Problem 9.1. Determine for which pairs of disjoint zero sequences A and B the subspace I(A) + I(B) is dense in L2_a(D).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ be the open unit disk and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ denote the Bergman space of holomorphic functions $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ that are square-integrable with respect to normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$, equipped with the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb{D}} f(z)\overline{g(z)}\,dA(z)$. A closed subspace $M\subset L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called invariant if $zM\subset M$. For a sequence $A=(a_n)$ of points of $\mathbb{D}$ (a "zero sequence") that is the zero set (with multiplicities) of some nonzero function in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$, define the zero-based invariant subspace
$$I(A)=\{f\in L^2_a(\mathbb{D}): f\text{ vanishes on }A\text{ (with multiplicities)}\}.$$
Given two disjoint zero sequences $A$ and $B$ in $\mathbb{D}$ for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$, characterize those pairs $(A,B)$ for which the algebraic sum
$$I(A)+I(B)=\{f+g: f\in I(A),\ g\in I(B)\}$$
is dense in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up a definitive characterization or resolution of the density of $I(A)+I(B)$ in the Bergman space for arbitrary disjoint zero sequences. There is a follow-up survey on recent progress and open problems on the Bergman space, but I could not verify from accessible sources that this particular problem has been fully resolved.
